lines.japanese:
背骨がギリギリと軋むような感覚がして、独りでに目が醒めた。
「あ………い、痛ぅ……………」
　ベッドから体を起こす。
　寝ぼけた頭のまま背中をさすると、背中にはこれといって傷はない。
　……痛みは背中ではなく、背骨から伝わってきていたみたいだ。
　それも痛みというより、何か熱い物が首の後ろあたりに溜まっていたような感じ。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish:
I wake on my own to the sensation of my spine grinding and creaking.
“Ah… o-ow…”
I sit up in bed. Still half asleep, I feel along my back, but there is no wound. The pain seems to have come from my spine rather than my back—and it was less a pain than the sensation of something hot pooling at the base of my neck.
lines.mao_english:

“Ah… o-ow…”
I sit up in bed. Still half asleep, I feel along my back, but there is no wound. The pain seems to have come from my spine rather than my back—and it was less a pain than the sensation of something hot pooling at the base of my neck.
lines.mirrorMoon:
A wrenching pain suddenly wakes me.
"Ah……… Ouch………"
I lift myself up from bed.
I sleepily check my back.
There aren't any wounds.
…… The pain is exactly my back, but more from my spine.
And not so much pain as it is the feeling of something hot welling up around the back of my neck.

lines.japanese:
「……寝違えたかな。
ベッドがふかふかなのはいいけど、こう立派すぎると――――」
　と。
　自分の手を見て、思考が止まった。
「―――――なんだ、これ」
　じっと両手を見つめる。
　赤い。
両手は肘のあたりから赤いペンキに塗れていて、掌は真っ赤になっていた。
　いや、赤というのは似つかわしくない。
　両手に付着したペンキは乾燥して、今では赤というより黒っぽかった。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Maybe I slept on it wrong. A soft bed is nice, but when it’s this extravagant…” Then I see my hands, and thought stops. “What… is this?”
I stare at both hands. Red. From the elbows down, my arms are smeared as though with red paint, my palms soaked crimson. No—red is no longer the right word. The paint has dried, and now it is closer to black.
lines.mao_english:
“…Maybe I slept on it wrong. A soft bed is nice, but when it’s this extravagant…” Then I see my hands, and thought stops. “What… is this?”
I stare at both hands. Red. From the elbows down, my arms are smeared as though with red paint, my palms soaked crimson. No—red is no longer the right word. The paint has dried, and now it is closer to black.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… I must've slept wrong.
It's a good thing this bed is soft, but when it's too gorgeous like this----"
All of a sudden…
I look down at my hands and my mind halts completely.
"-----What is, this?"
I stare at both hands.
Red.
From my elbows to my hands, my skin is painted red.
My fists are a dark vermillion.
No, red doesn't quite describe it.
The dried red on my hands is closer to black.

「あ、おはよう翡翠。

　なんとなく後ろめたくて、言い訳をしてみたりする。
「はい、おはようございます。
それでは着替えはいかがいたしましょう。
お部屋のほうに用意させていただきましたが」
　翡翠はすでに俺の部屋に行っていたらしい。
ちょうど階段で入れ違いになった、という事か。

I have laid out your clothes in your room.” Apparently Hisui has already been there. We must have passed each other on the stairs.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Besides, I don’t want you to change. It’s enough if, once in a very long while, some whim makes you rise early and join me like this.”
Akiha smiles and raises her cup to her lips. “Ugh…” A chill crawls down my spine. Something is wrong. A quiet, elegant, gentle Akiha should make me happy, but this is too much. And when something is strange, I cannot resist probing it.

lines.maoEnglish:
“And stop deciding my whole day for me! Why should I need your permission every time I choose to miss school?!” Akiha glares across the table, breathing hard. “……” I receive her fury with a grave expression and fold my arms. “There you are. If you have that much energy, then I suppose last night’s drinking really has worn off.”
“Ah…” Akiha makes the face of a squirrel caught eating a sugar confection, then knits her brows in a sulk.

lines.japanese:
「……兄さん。
今の、わざとですね」
「べつにー。
そう思ったのは本当の事だったけどな」
「手段が姑息です。
どうしてこう、ごく自然に穏やかな朝が演出できないんですか、兄さんは」
「おまえこそ。
平和な朝っていうのは演出するもんじゃないだろ。
……まあ、いつも待っていてくれた事は正直嬉しいよ。
　けどなんて言うかさ、秋葉とは喧々囂々とした朝を過ごしたほうが張り合いがあるんだから、言いたい事があったらじゃんじゃん言ってくれたほうが嬉しいんだ」
　……まあ、秋葉が本気で文句を言ってきたら遠野志貴は潰れてしまうので、そのあたり手加減してほしいとは思うんだが。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish: “…Brother. You did that deliberately.” “Not at all. I truly did think you were drunk.” “What an underhanded method. Why are you incapable of letting us enjoy one naturally peaceful morning?” “You’re the one trying to stage-manage it. Peaceful mornings shouldn’t need rehearsing. I honestly am happy that you’ve been waiting for me. But mornings with you feel more alive when we’re arguing. So if you have something to say, I’d rather you let me have it.” Admittedly, if Akiha ever unleashed her full arsenal of complaints, Shiki Tohno would be crushed flat. A little restraint would be appreciated.

"…… Nii-san, did you plan this?"
"Not really.
I actually did think that, though."
"Your method is a bit sneaky.
Why can't you just keep peaceful mornings peaceful, Nii-san?"
"Same to you.
A peaceful morning isn't something you control…… Well, I'm happy that you were always waiting for me though.

So go ahead and say the things you want to say."
…… Well, I'd probably be squashed completely if she really did say something every time she had a complaint, so I hope she can hold back at least a little.

“What about Akiha’s breakfast?” “Oh, Shiki. Miss Akiha has already eaten. If you want to have breakfast with her, you’ll need to wake before six.” That, unfortunately, will remain impossible for some time.

何事もなく教室について、いつものように授業が始まった。
「――――――――」

　弓塚の机はなくなっている、という事に。
　クラスメイトが一人いなくなってしまったぐらいで学校の時間割に変動はない。
　空席は空席のままではなく、空いてしまった机は埋められ、日常は普段通りに流れていく。

I reached the classroom without incident, and lessons began as usual.
“…” That was when I noticed. Yumizuka’s desk was gone. The school timetable did not change merely because one student had disappeared. No empty place was allowed to remain empty. The gap left by her desk had been filled, and everyday life flowed on undisturbed.

「……どう、して」
　気がついて、不安になった。
　弓塚との事は、決して忘れられない出来事のはずだった。

“Why…?” The realization left me uneasy. What had happened with Yumizuka should have been impossible to forget. So why—why had I never once tried to remember her until this very moment?
—You’re just like me, Shiki.
…Those words were still seared into my mind. “But… that’s strange.” And yet I could not make myself think about them deeply.

“…No. The person I borrowed it from didn’t seem to remember much about it. That isn’t the only reason, but I thought I might hold on to it a little longer.” “My, Shiki, are you planning to steal it for good? Surely it wasn’t anything so wonderful.” “Ha ha. No, it wasn’t. I borrowed it, but I never once found a use for it.”
…A man wearing a ribbon would only look unsettling, and fortunately I had never developed that particular taste.

lines.japanese:
「ふーん、そうですか。
……ねえ志貴さん。
志貴さんが借りた相手、というのを当ててみせましょうか？」
「いいけど。
琥珀さん、こういうの好きなんだね」
「はい。
それでですね、志貴さんが何かを借りた相手、というのはズバリ翡翠ちゃんでしょ」
「―――あたり。
よく解ったね、琥珀さん」
「だって八年前の事でしょう？
　その頃の志貴さんと仲が良かったのは翡翠ちゃんじゃないですか」
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hmm, I see. …Shiki, shall I guess who lent it to you?” “Go ahead. You really enjoy this sort of thing, don’t you?” “I do. And my answer is—Hisui.” “Right. How did you know?”
“It was eight years ago, wasn’t it? Hisui was the one you were close to back then, Shiki.”

lines.japanese:
「……そうだったかな。
けど仲が良かったはどうかは別にして、その約束は大事なものだったんだ。
　八年前のあの日。
今まで見ているだけだったあの子が返しに来てと言ってくれた。
……それだけで、遠野志貴は救われたんだよ」
「……………は？」
　ぴたりと。
　琥珀さんは、真面目な顔で俺を見た。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Were we? Whether we were close or not, that promise mattered to me. That day, eight years ago, the girl who had only ever watched me from a distance asked me to come back and return what she gave me. …That alone saved Shiki Tohno.”
“…What?” Kohaku froze. All levity vanished from her face as she looked at me.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… Is that so?
Putting that aside, the promise was a really important thing for me.
That day eight years ago, that girl, who only watched me, came to tell me to give it back…… That really saved me."
"………………… Huh?"
With a pause.
Kohaku looks directly at me.

「彼女にとってどうだったかは知らないけど、あの約束がなかったら俺は世の中を拗ねて、すごく捻くれたヤツになってた思う」
　……いらない子供として扱われたあの日。

“…”

lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「こんなのは自分だけのワガママなんだってわかってる。
けど、どうしても翡翠には返せない。
　このリボンを返す時は、相手にも覚えていてほしい。
本当に嬉しかったから、ありがとうってお礼を言って、きちんと約束を果たしたかった。
　……そうしないと俺は、あの時の翡翠にも、そのおかげでここにいる自分にも申し訳がたたない気がして」
　椅子に座ったまま、自分の中にだけ留めておくべき心情を吐露した。
　……どうして琥珀さんにこんな話をしてしまったのかは解らない。
　昨夜といい今といい、この庭にはなにか、過去を彷彿させるような効果でもあるのかもしれない。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish: “I know this is nothing but selfishness. But I can’t return it to Hisui. When I give the ribbon back, I want her to remember too. It made me so happy—I wanted to thank her and fulfill our promise properly. …Otherwise, I feel I’ll have betrayed both the Hisui of that day and the person I became because of her.” Still seated, I poured out feelings that should have remained mine alone. …I did not know why I had told Kohaku any of this. Between last night and now, perhaps this garden had some strange power to call up the past.
lines.mao_english: “I know this is nothing but selfishness. But I can’t return it to Hisui. When I give the ribbon back, I want her to remember too. It made me so happy—I wanted to thank her and fulfill our promise properly. …Otherwise, I feel I’ll have betrayed both the Hisui of that day and the person I became because of her.” Still seated, I poured out feelings that should have remained mine alone. …I did not know why I had told Kohaku any of this. Between last night and now, perhaps this garden had some strange power to call up the past.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"I know it's just my selfish notion, but I can't give it back to Hisui yet.
I want her to remember it.
Since it made me so happy, I want to thank her and fulfill the promise.
…… If I don't do that, I don't think I will be able to face myself or Hisui."
Still sitting in the chair, I completely bare my heart.
…… I don't know why I'm telling all of this to Kohaku-san.
Maybe there's something about this garden that helps me to talk about the past.

「……なんだよそれ。

「はい。

　その中でも秋葉さまの病状は軽い方なんです。
楽観はできませんが、志貴さんと違って決して命に関わる物ではありませんから、そう怖い顔をしないでくださいな」
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish: “…What is that supposed to mean? Akiha has always looked perfectly healthy.” “Yes, but everyone in the Tohno family suffers from some such complaint. Whether it is a hereditary defect or something else, Miss Akiha, Shiki, and your father have all been subject to physical attacks of one kind or another. Miss Akiha’s condition is among the milder cases. It cannot be dismissed, but unlike yours it poses no danger to her life, so please don’t look so frightened.”

lines.maoEnglish:
“…I’m sorry. Please take care of Akiha, Kohaku.” I bowed to her and walked away from Akiha’s room.
“…” Even back in my room, sleep was impossible. The sight of Akiha frightened of something had burned itself behind my eyelids, and my heart refused to settle.
“Ow…” The wounds on my back stung. Blood had seeped from the places Akiha’s nails had raked. They had split the skin and left dozens of marks like slashes from a box cutter. …But those wounds hardly hurt at all.

　なら―――正気じゃなかった遠野志貴も、自分である事に間違いはない。

lines.maoEnglish: It was monstrous. The person in that dream had not been sane. He was utterly different from the self standing here now. But Shiki Tohno had dreamed it. Therefore the mad Shiki Tohno had also, unquestionably, been me.

That is different from this me right now.
But, that's a dream that Tohno Shiki saw.

The room lurched around me.

“…Oh.” This time, it seemed I had failed.

When I thought about it, Hisui only appeared expressionless. Her feelings were often quite plain. Compared with the girl who had always sat by the window eight years ago, her face now revealed so much that it was almost disconcerting.

Hisui laid the uniform on my desk and walked soundlessly toward the door.

lines.maoEnglish:
Breakfast scarcely had a taste. What Kohaku had told me about my father spun endlessly through my head, and before I knew it I was standing at the mansion gates.
“You haven’t forgotten anything, have you, Shiki?” Since Hisui had shut herself in her room, Kohaku had come to see me off instead.
“Honestly, Shiki! The weather is beautiful today, so you must show a little more spirit. I can’t possibly send you out looking like that.” “Ah—right. …Sorry. I was thinking.” I shook my head lightly, trying to dislodge the shadow lodged there.

lines.mirrorMoon:
I ate breakfast, but I didn't taste anything.
What Kohaku-san said about my old man kept circling in my head and before I knew it, I was at the gate in front of the mansion.
"Shiki-san, you didn't forget anything?"
Hisui-chan is still in her room, Kohaku-san says as she sends me off.
"Geez, Shiki-san!
The weather is so nice today so you have to cheer up.
I can't send you off when you look like that."
"Ah---yeah.
…… You're right.
Sorry, I was just thinking about some things."
Giving my head a little shake, I banish the shadows in my mind.

lines.japanese:
「あ、少しはいつもの志貴さんに戻ってくれましたね。
はい、これなら安心です」
　……不思議だ。
　こう、まっすぐに笑顔を向けられると、本当に元気になれるような気がする。
「いってらっしゃい志貴さん。
お帰り、お待ちしておりますね」
　ぺこり、とお辞儀をする琥珀さん。
　それで、さっきまで自分を支配していた暗い感情は消えてくれた。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish:
“There—you look a little more like yourself again, Shiki. Now I can stop worrying.” …How strange. When she smiled at me so openly, I felt as though strength truly returned.
“Have a good day, Shiki. I’ll be waiting for you to come home.” Kohaku bowed, and the dark feelings that had ruled me until that moment disappeared.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Ah, now that's more like the normal Shiki-san.
Yes, I can relax now."
…… That's odd.
Seeing that smile, I really do feel better.
"Goodbye, Shiki-san.
I'll be waiting for your return."
Kohaku-san bows.
With that, all of my worries seem to disappear.

lines.japanese:
「――サンキュ、琥珀さん。
おかげで元気が出た」
「はい。
志貴さんにはやっぱり、明るいお顔が似合っていますから」
「……ありがとう。
それじゃ行ってきます、琥珀さん」
　心からのお礼を言って、学校に向かって走り出した。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish:
“Thanks, Kohaku. I feel much better.” “Good. A bright face suits you best, Shiki.” “…Thank you. I’m off, then.”
I thanked her from my heart and set off at a run for school.

lines.japanese:
いつもより余裕をもって教室に着いた。
　有彦は今日も遅刻らしく、おかげで静かにホームルームを迎えられる。
　かすかに騒がしい教室の中、席に座って担任がくるのを待つ事にした。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish: I reached the classroom with more time to spare than usual. Arihiko seemed to be late again, which meant I could greet homeroom in peace. I sat amid the low classroom chatter and waited for our teacher.

lines.japanese:
―――何のトラブルもなく一日が終わった。
　旅にでも出ているのか、有彦は欠席だった。
　旅、とは比喩表現でもなんでもなく、あいつは突発的に旅行に出かける、という奇癖をもっている。
　それもバイクに乗って気ままに放浪する、という格好のいいものではない。
平日のツアーパックは安いんだ、とご年配の方々にまぎれての観光旅行らしい。
　……まったく。
小学校からの付き合いになるが、あいつの趣味はいまいち掴めない。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish: The day ended without incident. Arihiko was absent, perhaps off traveling. That was not a figure of speech; he had the peculiar habit of taking sudden trips. Nor did he do anything glamorous, like roaming wherever his motorcycle carried him. Weekday package tours were cheap, he said, so apparently he joined sightseeing groups full of elderly travelers. …I had known him since elementary school, and still could not make sense of his tastes.
lines.mao_english: The day ended without incident. Arihiko was absent, perhaps off traveling. That was not a figure of speech; he had the peculiar habit of taking sudden trips. Nor did he do anything glamorous, like roaming wherever his motorcycle carried him. Weekday package tours were cheap, he said, so apparently he joined sightseeing groups full of elderly travelers. …I had known him since elementary school, and still could not make sense of his tastes.
lines.mirrorMoon:
---The day passes without any trouble.
Maybe he went on a trip?
Arihiko didn't show up.
"Trip" isn't a metaphor or anything.
He does have this strange habit of spontaneously taking trips.
It isn't anything cool like roaming the country on a motorcycle.
He goes on sightseeing tours on weekdays with the old people.
…… Geez.
I've known since elementary school, but I've never completely understood his hobbies.

lines.japanese:
――――屋敷に帰ってきた。
　学校にいる間は考えないようにしていた事が脳裏をよぎる。
　朝、琥珀さんが話してくれた親父の二面性。
　遠野家の人間が持つという、遺伝的な疾患。
　……翡翠の言うとおり、屋敷に帰ってきてからの俺はどこかおかしい。
　なにか、自分でも解らない所で記憶が曖昧になっている気がする。
　……琥珀さんの言っていたように、自分があの親父と同じとは思えない。
　だが事実として、この屋敷に帰ってきてから、俺は遠野志貴という自分に自信が持てなくなりつつある。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish:
I returned to the mansion.
The thoughts I had suppressed at school returned. My father’s two faces, as Kohaku had described them that morning. The hereditary afflictions of the Tohno family. …Hisui was right. Something had been wrong with me since I returned here. Somewhere beyond my own awareness, my memories seemed to be growing indistinct. …As Kohaku said, I could not believe I was the same as my father. Yet the fact remained: since returning to this mansion, I had begun to lose faith in the person called Shiki Tohno.

lines.japanese:
「本当に―――親父はおかしかったのか」
　確かにそんな記憶もあるが、はっきりとは断定できない。
　こんな事を気にするなんて自分でも馬鹿げていると解っている。
　だが、それでも―――遠野志貴は、遠野家というものについて知っておくべきなのかもしれない。
lines.label: s416
lines.maoEnglish: “Was there really something wrong with Father?” I had memories that supported it, but nothing clear enough to be certain. I knew it was ridiculous to obsess over this. Even so—perhaps Shiki Tohno needed to learn the truth about the Tohno family.
lines.mao_english: “Was there really something wrong with Father?” I had memories that supported it, but nothing clear enough to be certain. I knew it was ridiculous to obsess over this. Even so—perhaps Shiki Tohno needed to learn the truth about the Tohno family.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Was my old man---really that crazy?"

I understand that it's stupid of me to even be troubled by it.
But, still---I should probably know about the Tohno family.

　考えてみると、これはいい機会かもしれない。
